title: Protect people: their data, your voice and respect at work

say: Protect people: their data, your voice, and respect at work.
This is the video for module three of Ethics and Accountability at Work.
Personal data is any information that identifies a living person: a name with a phone number, an address, a photo, a BVN, bank details or health information.
In Nigeria, the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 sets the rules, and the Nigeria Data Protection Commission enforces them.

panel.heading: Before you share personal data
items: Do they need it?
Is this the purpose it was collected for?
Is it only the minimum?
Is the channel secure?

say: Before you share anyone's data, ask four questions. Do they need it? Is this the purpose? Is it the minimum? Is the channel secure?
And never post personal details, debts or health information in a group chat.

say: For example, Joy is secretary of a 60-member thrift and credit society in Owerri. The chairperson asks her to post the defaulters, with amounts and phone numbers, on the WhatsApp group to shame them into paying.
Joy runs the checklist. Do all 60 members need this? No. Is shaming the purpose the data was collected for? No.

panel.heading: Joy and the debtors' list
right: Full list in a protected sheet

say: So she suggests private messages to each defaulter, with the amount and the agreed repayment date. The group hears only totals: 420,000 naira outstanding across 7 loans.
The full list stays in a password-protected sheet shared only with the treasurer and chairperson.

say: A breach is when personal data is lost, stolen, or shared with the wrong people, like a spreadsheet sent to the wrong WhatsApp group. First, contain it. Delete the message for everyone, remove link access, or change the password.

panel.heading: If personal data goes astray
items: Contain it: delete, remove access, change password
Tell your manager at once, in writing
Note what data and how many people
Follow procedure: serious cases reach NDPC in 72 hours

say: Tell your manager or the person responsible for data immediately, in writing.

say: Under the Act, organisations must notify the Commission within 72 hours of a breach likely to pose a high risk to people. Hiding it only makes it worse.

panel.rule: Never hide a data breach. Report it quickly.

say: Speaking up means raising a concern about wrongdoing that affects others. First, write down what you saw, with dates, amounts and who was present.
For example, Esther works in accounts at an NGO in Jos. The same supplier invoice for 1,200,000 naira has been paid twice. She does not assume fraud. It could be an error.

panel.heading: The escalation ladder
items: Your supervisor or chairperson
A senior manager, HR or another executive
The board, trustees or a general meeting
External bodies such as EFCC or ICPC

say: Start at the lowest safe level. Esther emails the facts to her finance manager, who is not involved.

say: Nothing happens for three weeks. She follows up once, then uses the next level in her organisation's policy.

say: The policy names the board audit committee chair, so she sends the same calm summary there, marked confidential. The money is recovered.

say: For criminal matters or public money, external bodies such as the EFCC and ICPC exist. Never post accusations on social media. And if you fear for your physical safety, put that first.

panel.rule: Write facts, not opinions. Report in writing and keep copies.

say: Everyone has the right to work without being humiliated, threatened or pressured. The key word is unwanted. Meant as a joke is no excuse. What matters is the effect.

cards.d: A promotion, contract or loan made to depend on a date or sexual favour.
Repeated sexual jokes, comments on a woman's body, explicit images in the office group.
Shouting at someone in front of customers, impossible deadlines, mocking her accent or tribe.

say: Quid pro quo means this for that: when a promotion, a contract or a loan approval is made to depend on a sexual favour.

say: Bullying is repeated intimidation: shouting at someone in front of customers, or mocking her accent or tribe. If it happens to you, write down each incident, screenshot messages, and report in writing. You are not to blame.

say: When you see someone being harassed, you can help without putting yourself in danger. Use the 5Ds.

panel.heading: The 5Ds: how bystanders can help
items: Distract: interrupt indirectly
Delegate: get someone with authority
Document: note what happens, if safe
Delay: check on her afterwards
Direct: speak up briefly, if safe

say: Distract. For example: Madam Ada, the customer is asking for you.

say: Delegate. Get a supervisor, security staff or the chairperson.

say: Document. If it is safe, note what happens and give it to the person affected. Never post it without her permission.

say: Delay. Afterwards, ask her: are you okay? How can I help?

say: Direct. If it is safe, say briefly: that is not okay. And remember, punishing anyone for a complaint made in good faith is itself serious misconduct.

Then plan one 5D action for a place you work or meet. Now continue with the lessons below.
